title: fix: macOS Gateway stop reports success before shutdown completes
body:
Related: #153704 (comment 6). Thanks @britrik for reporting the macOS shutdown and repair-admission failure.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS Gateway stop reporting success before it has proved that the LaunchAgent is unloaded and its process has exited, followed by repair refusals that do not name the stop command.

## User Impact

`openclaw gateway stop` and `openclaw gateway stop --disable` now unload the LaunchAgent through launchd and verify shutdown before reporting success. `--disable` still preserves the disabled policy across logins. Failed shutdown reports the exact native command and required macOS session; update/repair admission names the profile-aware managed-service stop command and explains an incomplete shutdown when stop already returned successfully.

## Why This Change Was Made

The default stop owner accepted bootout and checked only the Gateway port. The separate disable-plus-stop path could deliberately leave the job loaded, which fails the update publication precondition even with no current process. Both modes now share bootout and verification of the unloaded label plus the original and subsequently observed service PIDs. Running states without a verifiable PID fail explicitly. Delegated update authority is rechecked after awaited work and before native writes or stale-process cleanup. The redundant stopped-state poll, fallback branches, and retired mutation mode are removed.

The service lifecycle owner remains `src/daemon/launchd-stop.ts`. Candidate Doctor diagnostics use the existing refusal-formatting owner and the activation markers already set by released update drivers. Standalone repair retains its existing stop/restore custody. Detached update handoffs retain their separate parent-exit contract and existing unload verification; this change does not alter update backups, rollback, or schemas.

## Evidence

**Compatibility disposition:** Skip “Add data-model compatibility proof” as not applicable: no persisted data model, schema, migration, backup, or restoration policy is touched. The launchd stop owner’s verification and the refusal text are runtime/diagnostic changes, so no data-model compatibility proof applies. [ClawSweeper revision 4 (18:48Z)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153789#issuecomment-5750779427) itself states: “No schema, migration, persisted representation, backup, or restoration policy changes support the previous generic migration-proof blocker.”

Initial implementation validation covered 429 passing tests across eight files; affected owners were rerun after those edits. Regressions were demonstrated failing before their corresponding fixes, including loaded labels, surviving or missing PIDs, late handoff revocation, and missing recovery commands.

| Boundary | Passing tests |
| --- | ---: |
| LaunchAgent lifecycle and native stop fences | 200 |
| Gateway CLI, repair history, and maintenance | 166 |
| Runtime publication | 38 |
| Released-driver Doctor admission and recovery | 16 |
| Native update handoff authority | 9 |

The initial implementation passed all selected `check:changed` gates. The wrapper passed through typechecks and dead-export scans, then reported one local `no-shadow` naming error. After the behavior-neutral rename, the exact core lint command and every remaining schema, storage, sidecar, import-cycle, webhook, and pairing guard passed individually. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass.

Independent Codex review completed. Its missing-PID finding was fixed and regression-tested. The final callback warning was checked and rejected: the unload loop receives the original synchronous `GatewayServiceControlArgs.assertCurrent`; the asynchronous `assertStopCurrent` calls before writes and port cleanup are awaited.

Live macOS 27.0 arm64 / Node 26.8.2 proof used session-owned `ai.openclaw.l1038-*` LaunchAgents, isolated state directories, free loopback ports, and a synthetic listener with delayed SIGTERM exit. This exercised the real native stop owner; CLI dispatch is covered by the lifecycle tests.

| Native stop proof | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default stop with delayed exit | Unloaded; PID gone | Unloaded; PID gone |
| `--disable` with quick exit | Reported success while label remained loaded | Unloaded; PID gone |
| `--disable` with six-second drain | Not run | Unloaded; PID gone |

All test LaunchAgents were cleaned up and their original PIDs verified gone. The reporter's exact unchanged-PID default-stop behavior was not reproduced on this host; deterministic regressions cover successful bootout that leaves the label loaded or the original PID alive. Testbox macOS is unavailable. No operator Gateway or operator state was used.

Production: **+134 / −116 (net +18)**. Tests and test support: **+238 / −166 (net +72)**. Docs: **+12 / −1**. No options, dependency, schema, or release-artifact changes.

### Receipt-compensation CI follow-up

Head `10432e980dcd24c93d4b37ce4bd1d84842dcb33c` rebases the original patch without changes onto `9f5048ae99634aae961fe9995d1aac542eca6739` and corrects the receipt fixture's process model. Its synthetic launchctl PID 42 had leaked into the host process table, so CI could observe an unrelated live PID even after fake bootout. The fixture now models its process alive while loaded and dead after completed bootout, with the contract documented inline. Production's bounded verification and refusal remain unchanged, as do all receipt/input-order assertions.

The same 31-second failure was reproduced before the fixture correction. Afterward, all 290 targeted tests passed across the receipt-backup, receipt-ordering, launchd, stop-fence, and native update-handoff suites. Targeted core lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed; fresh Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P2. The caller audit covered the Darwin service and node adapters, CLI stop/uninstall paths, update maintenance, receipt restoration, and native/fixture tests; no other fake-PID mismatch was found. Follow-up LOC: **0 production, +3 test, 0 deleted**.

### ClawSweeper checklist disposition

The September 20 16:59 UTC review of `10432e980dcd24c93d4b37ce4bd1d84842dcb33c` has no actionable findings and no separate Rank-up moves. Its remaining “Add data-model compatibility proof” checklist item is skipped as inapplicable: the cited repair and Doctor changes only improve refusal diagnostics; they do not change stored data, schemas, admission predicates, migration, backup, rollback, or restoration ownership. The review itself confirms that the generic migration warning is unsupported by the diff. Existing released-driver marker fixtures and the 16 passing Doctor admission/recovery tests cover compatibility with installed update drivers; the receipt-compensation follow-up retains all input-restoration ordering assertions. The native default-stop reproduction limitation remains disclosed above.

The September 20 17:37 UTC re-review of the same head confirms this checklist disposition, reports no actionable findings, and adds no Rank-up moves. Its generic compatibility checklist remains skipped for the same source-backed reasons.

The September 20 19:09 UTC ClawSweeper revision 5 reviews the exact same head and again reports no actionable findings or separate Rank-up moves. Its sole “Add data-model compatibility proof” checklist item is skipped: the review confirms that Doctor, publication, and repair changes alter diagnostics rather than admission predicates or storage contracts. No schema, migration, backup, rollback, or restoration policy changes require additional data-model proof. The native default-stop reproduction limitation remains disclosed above.

The September 20 19:51 UTC ClawSweeper revision 6 reviews the same head, reports no actionable correctness findings, and adds no Rank-up moves. Its sole generic data-model compatibility checklist remains skipped: the review confirms that the diff changes shutdown verification and refusal diagnostics without changing admission predicates, stored representations, schemas, migration, backup, rollback, or restoration policy. The native default-stop reproduction limitation remains disclosed above.
